findings.claim: A real manifest served with the wrong Content-Type is silently treated as 'absent', suppressing all published documents without any loud signal
findings.evidence: fetch.cljs:47-48 maps ANY 2xx response with content-type text/html to {:fetch/status :absent}. The contract (lines 40-43) explicitly warns that static servers do not know the .edn extension; if a host serves a VALID manifest.edn as text/html instead of application/edn, the reader renders 'nothing published' rather than failing loudly — the swallowed-error asymmetry the contract's reader table exists to prevent. The infra parse layer's markup check (published_manifest.cljs:38-40) would catch an HTML body, but never runs because the content-type short-circuits first. This is a deliberate, documented trade (needed so an SPA-fallback shell for a missing file reads as absent), and the application/edn serving requirement is correctly escalated to open-hax/services in the followups — but the loud/quiet asymmetry the contract mandates is only as strong as the host's content-type config.

findings.claim: Published artifact HTML is injected as innerHTML of a div, so the contract's full-document artifact ('<!doctype html>…' with head, title, meta) loses everything outside the body
findings.evidence: published.cljs:73-74 uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML with the raw :artifact/body. The contract's PublicationArtifact example (line 65) is a complete HTML document. innerHTML parsing discards doctype/html/head, so an artifact carrying its own <title>, <meta>, or stylesheet link renders without them. Not a contract violation (rendering is reader-side discretion) and the namespace docstring acknowledges the trust boundary, but the Knoxx writer being built against this contract right now may reasonably assume its document head survives.

findings.claim: Docstring/behaviour mismatch: listing does not fall back to the document id
findings.evidence: published.cljc:151 docstring says 'a route without one falls back to its document id', but listing returns :listing/title nil and the view (sections/published.cljs:31) falls back to the :published/untitled message instead; :listing/document is never rendered. Behaviour is fine; the docstring describes a different function.

findings.claim: sections/published_test.cljs asserts only fn?, the exact assertion strength render_test.cljs's docstring criticizes
findings.evidence: The whole file is two deftests of (is (fn? ...)). render_test.cljs lines 4-7 explicitly argue fn? proves nothing — and then covers these components properly, so this is redundancy rather than a coverage hole, but the weak test file adds no signal and slightly undercuts the repo's own stated standard.

result.contract_conformance: Conformant on every checkable reader rule, each with a real assertion, re-run by me: manifest absent -> :ok/not-an-error (law decode of ::absent plus fetch-edge 404 test); empty :manifest/routes -> same as absent; unknown fields ignored AND dropped from decoded routes (an-unknown-field-is-ignored-and-dropped); each missing required route field (:route/path, :route/locale, :route/artifact, :route/media-type) fails loudly per-field (a-missing-required-field-fails-loudly loops over required-route-keys); missing/unsupported :manifest/version fails loudly; selector keyword :route/revision rejected with the offending value named; cross-origin/absolute artifact URLs rejected before any fetch (cross-origin-artifact fixture, plus fetch.cljs refusing non-relative paths without making a request); loudness is user-visible via a role=alert banner rendering the site's own sections underneath (render_test an-invalid-manifest-renders-a-loud-alert-not-a-blank-page asserts the field name appears); default locale at /, prefix routing, unknown prefix -> default not 404; manifest shape, EDN, namespaced keys, and fixture bytes match the contract example exactly (fixture table double-checked against on-disk EDN files by infra test). The 'locale carries no routes -> not offered in the switcher' rule is implemented for document views (manifest-derived options, tested) while site pages offer all compiled locales — a documented, defensible reading given the contract's two-content-sources section. The application/edn serving requirement and /published/ fallback exclusion are correctly identified as services-side duties and escalated as followups, since the website cannot enforce them.
